name: Button
description: A button triggers an action in place: saving a form, opening a dialog, deleting an item. Variants signal what kind of action it is, appearances set how much attention it draws, and sizes fit it to the density of the surrounding UI. IconButton is the icon-only form for compact, well-known actions.
whenToUse: To trigger an action on the current page: submit, save, confirm, open, delete.
To let people commit to a decision in a dialog or form.
IconButton: for compact, widely recognized actions (close, edit, more) in toolbars, cards and table rows.

whenNotToUse.text: To navigate to another page or URL.
To switch a setting on or off.
To pick one option from a small set of views.
For an icon whose meaning is not obvious without text.
whenNotToUse.alternative: Button with iconStart and a label

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The clickable area. Its fill, outline and corner radius come from the variant, appearance and radius theme.

anatomy.name: Start icon
anatomy.description: Optional icon before the label; replaced by the spinner while loading.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Short verb or verb phrase that says what happens.

anatomy.name: End icon
anatomy.description: Optional icon after the label, often a chevron or external-link arrow.

anatomy.name: Focus ring
anatomy.description: Outline shown when the button is reached with the keyboard.

values.meaning: The main action on a screen or in a dialog. Use one per view.
Supporting actions next to a primary one, e.g. Cancel beside Save.
Confirms a positive, completing action, e.g. Approve or Publish.
Destructive or irreversible actions, e.g. Delete account.
Actions that need caution but are not destructive, e.g. Override.
Highest emphasis. Solid fill in the variant color.
Medium emphasis. Variant-colored outline and text, tinted on hover.
Low emphasis for toolbars and dense UI. No outline until hovered.
Lowest emphasis, link-like. Underlined text for inline actions.
Prominent calls to action, e.g. on a landing page hero.

states.name: Hover
states.meaning: Shows the button responds to the pointer.

states.name: Focus
states.trigger: Reached with Tab (:focus-visible); adds the focus ring.

states.name: Pressed
states.trigger: While pressed with pointer or keyboard (:active).

states.name: Disabled
states.meaning: The action is not available right now.

states.name: Loading
states.meaning: The action is running; clicks are ignored until it finishes.

behavior.text: Defaults to type="button" so it never submits a form by accident. Pass type="submit" for a form’s submit button.
The spinner replaces the start icon and the label stays, so the width does not jump. The button keeps focus and is announced as busy.
Labels do not wrap. Keep them short; in narrow layouts use fullWidth so the button fills its container.
Padding and icons use logical positions, so the start icon sits on the right in Arabic.
Colors follow brand and mode, padding follows density, corners follow the radius theme.

content: Start with a verb that says what happens: "Save changes", "Delete file", "Send invite".
Keep labels to one to three words; use sentence case.
Match the words people saw earlier in the flow, e.g. "Delete" in the button of a "Delete project?" dialog.

guidelines.do: Use one filled primary button per view for the main action.
guidelines.dont: Place several filled primary buttons side by side.
guidelines.why: Competing primary actions make it unclear what to do next.

guidelines.do: Pair a primary action with secondary or outline buttons for alternatives.
guidelines.dont: Style Cancel as a filled primary button.
guidelines.why: Visual weight should follow importance; the safe path should not look like the main action.

guidelines.do: Use the danger variant for destructive actions and confirm them in a dialog.
guidelines.dont: Use danger just to make a button stand out.
guidelines.why: Red signals risk; overusing it teaches people to ignore it.

guidelines.do: Give every IconButton a label that says what it does.
guidelines.dont: Rely on an unfamiliar icon alone.
guidelines.why: Screen readers announce the label, and sighted users see it as a tooltip.

guidelines.do: Use a Link for navigation to another page.
guidelines.dont: Use a Button to change the URL.
guidelines.why: Links and buttons behave differently for keyboard, screen readers and "open in new tab".

keyboard.action: Moves focus to and from the button.

aria.when: Set automatically while loading, so the button stays focusable.
Set automatically on IconButton from its label prop.
Icons are decorative; the label carries the meaning.

accessibility.focus: A visible focus ring (brand accent, at least 3:1 against the background) appears when the button is reached with the keyboard. Disabled buttons are skipped by Tab; loading buttons keep focus.

wcag.how: Label text meets 4.5:1 in every variant, appearance, state, brand and mode (checked in CI).
Focus ring and outline strokes meet 3:1.
Native button: reachable with Tab, activated with Enter and Space.
Every size is at least 24×24 px.
Label or aria-label names the button; busy and disabled states are exposed.

notes: Do not put interactive elements inside a button.
If a button opens a menu or dialog, the menu/dialog component sets aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.

examples.description: The default button: filled, primary, medium.

related.relation: Icon-only form of Button, exported alongside it.
Use for navigation instead of a button.

changes: New variants success, danger and warning; new appearances outline and ghost; new size large.
Renamed buttonStyle to appearance; removed the state prop in favor of real hover, focus and pressed states.
Added iconStart, iconEnd, loading, fullWidth and the IconButton component.
Defaults to type="button"; keyboard focus ring; WCAG AA contrast in every theme.
First version: primary and secondary, filled and text, small and medium.
Filled buttons in dark mode use a darker fill with light text (new --color-bg-accent-{tone}-strong-* roles); AA contrast in every brand.

components.name: Button
components.description: Triggers an action. Use a link instead when it navigates to another page.

variant.description:
What kind of action this is. `primary` for the main action on a screen, `secondary`
for supporting actions, `success` to confirm a positive outcome, `danger` for
destructive actions, `warning` for actions that need caution.

appearance.description:
Visual weight. `filled` for the most important action, `outline` for secondary
emphasis, `ghost` for low emphasis in toolbars and dense UI, `text` for inline,
link-like actions.

size.description: `small` for dense UI, `medium` by default, `large` for prominent calls to action.

iconStart.description: Icon before the label (after it in right-to-left languages). Hidden from screen readers.

iconEnd.description: Icon after the label (before it in right-to-left languages). Hidden from screen readers.

loading.description:
Shows a spinner and ignores clicks while an action runs. The button stays focusable
and is announced as busy.

fullWidth.description: Stretches the button to the full width of its container.

components.name: IconButton
components.description:
A button that shows only an icon. Use it for compact, well-known actions (close, edit,
delete) where an icon is understood without text.

label.description:
What the button does, e.g. "Delete message". Required: it is the accessible name
screen readers announce and the tooltip sighted users see, since there is no
visible text.

variant.description:
What kind of action this is. `primary` for the main action on a screen, `secondary`
for supporting actions, `success` to confirm a positive outcome, `danger` for
destructive actions, `warning` for actions that need caution.

appearance.description:
Visual weight. `filled` for the most important action, `outline` for secondary
emphasis, `ghost` for low emphasis in toolbars and dense UI, `text` for inline,
link-like actions.

size.description: `small` for dense UI, `medium` by default, `large` for prominent calls to action.

Shows a spinner and ignores clicks while an action runs. The button stays focusable
and is announced as busy.
